task.name: Sprint that dies on an unhandled exception is reported as completed, with killed stories still shown running
task.story_text:
## Observed behavior

A sprint that terminates on an unhandled exception is reported as `completed`,
with the stories it killed still displayed as `running`.

Run `f13f739e19c3` (`issues-1972,1946,1945,1934`, 2026-07-26) raised a
`RuntimeError` out of `run_sprint` and died. The process was gone; two agent
process groups were left orphaned and reaped by the next command:

```
[forge] 21:41:16.746   reaping orphaned agent process group pgid=49573 (owner sprint pid=75345 is dead, ...issue-1972)
[forge] 21:41:16.746   reaping orphaned agent process group pgid=64074 (owner sprint pid=75345 is dead, ...issue-1934)
```

`forge status` nonetheless printed:

```
Sprint: issues-1972,1946,1945,1934  run: f13f739e19c3  [completed]  cost: $3.75
▸ #1945  running   WORKSPACE   8m   creating workspace
▸ #1972  running   DEV         21m  running
```

Two stories were reported as in progress by a process that no longer existed,
under a sprint labelled `completed`. No error, no cause, and no indication that
anything had terminated abnormally.

Immediately before this, `forge status --watch` reported `No live sprint runs`,
which was accurate. The two surfaces disagreed, and the one that reads as more
authoritative was the wrong one.

## Diagnosis

**Observed symptom:** a crashed sprint presented as a completed sprint with live
stories.

**Evidence.** The terminating exception is in the run log:

```
Sprint error: Broken baseline: configured gate failed on sprint merge base
6911e52970d352b189d4856a8344c3c8cd3185d2 before any dev work started (Gate returned FAIL)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../theforge/cli/sprint.py", line 1132, in _run_query_mode
    result = run_sprint(
  File ".../theforge/sprint/runner.py", line 1856, in run_sprint
    raise RuntimeError(str(baseline_gate.get("message", "Broken baseline")))
```

`run_sprint` raises at `src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:1856` and the exception
propagates out of `_run_query_mode` at `src/theforge/cli/sprint.py:1132`. The
per-story state written before the raise still records `#1945` at `WORKSPACE`
and `#1972` at `DEV`, and nothing rewrites those entries on the exception path.

**Ruled out — the sprint having actually completed.** The owning pid (75345)
was dead at the time of the status call, which is what triggered the orphan
reaping quoted above, and `--watch` independently reported no live run.

**Ruled out — duplicate of #1906 or #1972.** Those concern how *completed* work
is labelled and costed: resume-skipped stories grouped under `LANDED`, and cost
lost across a re-exec. Both presuppose a run that finished. This is a run that
did not finish being reported as one that did, which is a distinct claim and
survives either fix.

**Confirmed cause:** sprint termination status is derived from state that is
only advanced on the normal completion path. An exception escaping `run_sprint`
leaves the last-written phase as the terminal record, so stories retain their
in-flight status and the sprint is classified by absence of an explicit failure
rather than by presence of a successful end.

**Fix-success criterion:** a sprint whose process terminates on an unhandled
exception is reported with a status distinct from a normal completion, carrying
the terminating cause, and the stories that were in flight are shown as
interrupted rather than running. Given run `f13f739e19c3` as input, the status
names the broken-baseline error and does not read `completed`, and `#1945` and
`#1972` are not described as running.

## Expected behavior

A run's reported disposition has to be derived from how it actually ended, not
from the absence of a record saying otherwise. Treating "no completion marker
was written" as equivalent to "completed" makes the most severe outcomes the
least visible, because the failures most likely to skip the bookkeeping are the
ones that terminate the process abruptly. An operator reading a terminal status
is entitled to assume that status was written by something that observed the
ending.

The same applies to per-item state within the run. Work that was interrupted is
not work that is progressing, and presenting it as in flight invites an operator
to wait on a process that cannot advance it. Where the system cannot determine
what happened to an item, saying that is serviceable; carrying forward the last
known phase as though it were current is not, because it is indistinguishable
from live progress.

Finally, two surfaces reporting on the same run must not contradict each other.
When one command reports no live run and another reports the same run as
completed with running stories, at least one is wrong, and the operator has no
basis for choosing between them.

handoff.summary: A sprint's terminal disposition is now derived from how it actually ended rather than from the absence of a completion record. detach.write_run_ended accepts a cause persisted as a second line in .forge/runs/<run_id>.ended, with read_run_ended_record() returning (outcome, cause) and legacy single-line markers still readable. Both sprint CLI paths (query mode and manifest mode) and cmd_run default to a failed disposition and record 'completed' only when the runner returns normally; an exception records 'failed' plus the terminating cause, and SIGINT records 'stopped'. The detached-path atexit backstop no longer hardcodes 'completed' — it writes the outcome this process observed, with a thin cmd_sprint wrapper recording failures that escape before the per-mode try/finally. On the read side, status_reader.mark_interrupted_entries() rewrites in-flight ('running') stories to 'interrupted' (last known phase preserved as history, detail annotated), applied by display_sprint_status whenever the owning PID is gone; the header prints the recorded cause. Both forge status and forge status --watch render through that single function, so they cannot disagree. Docs gained a run-disposition table.

commits.message: fix(status): report crashed sprints as failed with in-flight stories interrupted

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A sprint whose process terminates on an unhandled exception is reported with a status distinct from a normal completion, carrying the terminating cause.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Query mode, manifest mode, cmd_run, and the atexit backstop all write 'failed' with the exception type and message as cause; sprint status renders [failed] plus a 'cause:' line, and detach.read_run_status reports phase FAILED. Covered by test_query_mode_records_failed_outcome_with_cause, test_manifest_mode_records_failed_outcome_with_cause, test_cmd_run_records_failed_outcome_on_exception, test_backstop_records_failure_when_exception_escapes_cmd_sprint, test_read_run_status_reports_failed_phase.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Stories that were in flight when the sprint died are shown as interrupted rather than running.
acceptance_criteria.notes: mark_interrupted_entries() is applied in display_sprint_status on the not-live branch, so any story whose last recorded status was 'running' renders as 'interrupted' with its last phase retained in the PHASE column and detail rewritten to 'interrupted — sprint process is no longer running; last: <old>'. Covered by test_mark_interrupted_entries_rewrites_running_stories, test_crashed_sprint_status_names_cause_and_interrupts_stories, test_stopped_sprint_stories_are_interrupted_not_running, with test_live_sprint_still_reports_running guarding the live case.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given run f13f739e19c3 as input, the status names the broken-baseline error and does not read completed, and #1945 and #1972 are not described as running.
acceptance_criteria.notes: test_crashed_sprint_status_names_cause_and_interrupts_stories reconstructs that run's state file (#1945 WORKSPACE, #1972 DEV) plus the broken-baseline failed marker and asserts [failed] present, [completed] absent, 'Broken baseline' present, and no story described as running.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Two surfaces reporting on the same run must not contradict each other.
acceptance_criteria.notes: forge status and forge status --watch both render via display_sprint_status, which is the only place the reconciliation and terminal-outcome labelling happen — there is no second divergent code path. The watch overlay adds live per-frame cost deltas only, on runs whose PID is present.

story_deviations: Preflight scoped the fix to _run_query_mode; I applied the same correction to manifest-mode sprint (cli/sprint.py) and cmd_run (cli/run.py) since they are the identical unconditional-'completed' write and would otherwise reproduce the bug verbatim.

Also fixed the detached-path atexit backstop, which independently wrote 'completed' for exceptions escaping before the per-mode try/finally — a second instance of the same falsehood not named in the spec.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
